question:
A 72-year-old male patient seeks medical evaluation for progressive symptoms including nocturia,
fatigue, and exertional dyspnea. His exercise tolerance has decreased from 15 minutes to 5 minutes of
walking, and he now requires two pillows while sleeping to prevent orthopnea. His medical history
includes hypertension managed with amlodipine and prazosin, though he reports poor medication
adherence. Physical examination reveals: - Pulse: 75/min - Blood pressure: 150/90 mm Hg - Laterally
displaced apical heartbeat - 2+ bilateral lower leg pitting edema - S4 gallop - Fine bibasilar rales Which
pathophysiologic change is most likely to be present in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Increased
atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) levels (B) Decrease in left ventricular elastance (C) Decreased renal
perfusion pressure (D) Increased pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (E) Decreased systemic
vascular resistance (F) Decrease in total peripheral vascular resistance (G) Impaired diastolic
relaxation of the left ventricle (H) Constriction of efferent renal arterioles (I) Activation of the
renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) (J) Reduced myocardial oxygen delivery due to
coronary perfusion mismatch
 A. Reduced myocardial oxygen delivery due to coronary perfusion mismatch
B. Increased atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) levels
C. Decrease in total peripheral vascular resistance
D. Impaired diastolic relaxation of the left ventricle
E. Constriction of efferent renal arterioles
F. Decreased renal perfusion pressure
G. Decrease in left ventricular elastance
H. Decreased systemic vascular resistance
I. Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS)
J. Increased pulmonary capillary wedge pressure
